answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Consistency Rule. Each identity stores a behavioural delta between consecutive epochs; if drift exceeds a threshold, the identity's credit vault is frozen pending review. Enforcement compares action distributions, not just counts. Sybils must farm consistent behaviour across many epochs per identity, and each fake identity needs its own maintained vault plus a shale-thin history that review can expose. Attack cost scales linearly with identities and epochs.
